problem: In weak-texture environments (e.g., corridors and rooms with few visual features), visual feature extraction fails, and traditional high-precision maps incur large storage overhead unsuitable for storage-limited agents, which hurts navigation.
motivation: Embodied agents in IoT systems bridge the physical environment and digital services but often have limited storage. Humans understand environments through reasoning and selective information retention rather than dense mapping, which motivates a sparse, semantic, cognition-inspired map.
key_idea: Build a lightweight topological-semantic map (CogMap) that categorizes the environment into corridors and rooms, creates nodes in real time, and combines them with odometry for localization and occupancy map construction.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract suggests that semantic node categories (corridor/room) plus sparse nodes can replace dense maps while keeping navigation performance, giving better storage efficiency and node sparsity than mainstream topological maps.
method: Semantic environment categorization: divides the environment into corridors and rooms, inspired by human cognition
Real-time node creation: creates topological nodes online according to the semantic category
Odometry-based localization: nodes combined with odometry to localize the agent
Occupancy map construction: builds an occupancy map from nodes and odometry to form CogMap
Room-to-room navigation: a navigation method built on CogMap to validate the map

setting.observation: not specified (likely onboard visual sensing plus odometry)

results: The abstract states that CogMap outperforms mainstream topological maps in storage efficiency, navigation performance, and node sparsity. No numbers or named baselines are given.
limitations: Only room/corridor categories are used, which may not generalize to more varied environments
Evaluation details (simulator, real robot, baselines) are unknown from the abstract
